Three bundled skills work together to launch your app and confirm changes against the running app instead of just tests:

| Skill                  | Purpose                                                                                                           |

`/run` and `/verify` work without setup. They infer the launch from your project type (CLI, server, TUI, browser-driven) and from what's in your README, `package.json`, or `Makefile`. That inference gets unreliable for projects that need anything beyond a standard launch: a database, an env file, a graphical session, a multi-step build.

---
description: SQL team conventions
applyTo: *.sql
---

## Naming

- **Schemas:** `dbo` (core warehouse), `stg` (staging, always disposable), `etl` (load procedures), and `reporting` (read-only consumer-facing objects).
- **Tables:** `PascalCase`; dimensions are prefixed with `Dim`, and facts are prefixed with `Fact`.
- **Constraints:** `PK_`, `FK_`, `UQ_`, `DF_` (default), `CK_` (check), and `IX_`/`UX_` (index).
- Every object name is wrapped in brackets (`[brackets]`) in DDL to match the existing style.

## File header doc comment

- Every object file (`Tables/`, `Views/`, `Procedures/`, `Functions/`) starts with a top-of-file `/* ... */` block comment.
- Required fields: `Author` (name + email; get from `git config user.name`/`user.email` if unknown), `AI model` (if AI-assisted), `Created` date, a business-facing `Description`, and a `Change log`.
- `Change log` is a flat bullet list, one entry per change, in the form: `date | Ticket: <id or N/A> | author | model | description/commit message`. Newest entry last (append-only).
- Never invent a ticket number for a real change — use `N/A` if none exists.
- Add short (one line) inline comments next to columns/clauses whose intent isn't obvious from the code itself (e.g. a computed-elsewhere value, a non-obvious default, a temporal/system column). Don't restate what a line already says.

### Template

```sql
/*
    Author:      <Name> <email>
    AI model:    <model name, or omit if not AI-assisted>
    Created:     <YYYY-MM-DD>
    Description: <business usage — why this object exists, who consumes it>

    Change log:
    - <YYYY-MM-DD> | Ticket: <id|N/A> | <author> | <model|N/A> | <description/commit message>
*/
```

Created `audit-sql-headers.js`

**Input:**

- content:

```
export const meta = {
  name: 'audit-sql-headers',
  description: 'Audit every SQL object file in RetailDW for a compliant header doc comment (Author, AI model, Created, Description, Change log) per .github/instructions/sql-conventions.instruction.md',
}

const found = await agent(
  'List every .sql file under RetailDW/Tables/, RetailDW/Views/, RetailDW/Procedures/, and RetailDW/Functions/ in this repo. Return relative paths.',
  {
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      required: ['files'],
      properties: { files: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } },
    },
  },
)

const audits = await pipeline(found.files, file =>
  agent(
    `Read ${file} and check its top-of-file /* ... */ header comment against .github/instructions/sql-conventions.instruction.md. ` +
      'It must contain: Author (name + email), AI model (or an explicit note that none was used), a Created date, a business-facing ' +
      'Description, and an append-only Change log with at least one dated entry in the form ' +
      '"date | Ticket: <id|N/A> | author | model | description". Report any missing or malformed field. ' +
      'Do not invent a ticket number or author if one is not present in the file.',
    {
      label: file,
      schema: {
        type: 'object',
        required: ['file', 'compliant', 'issues'],
        properties: {
          file: { type: 'string' },
          compliant: { type: 'boolean' },
          issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
        },
      },
    },
  ),
)

// only report the files that need fixing
return audits.filter(a => a && !a.compliant)

```

Created `.claude/workflows/audit-sql-headers.js` — a Claude Code dynamic workflow (docs: [Orchestrate subagents at scale with dynamic workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows)).

What it does: fans out one subagent per `.sql` file under `RetailDW/Tables|Views|Procedures|Functions` to check the file's header doc-comment against the real convention in `.github/instructions/sql-conventions.instruction.md` (Author, AI model, Created, Description, Change log), then returns only the non-compliant files with their issues.

Run it in Claude Code with `/audit-sql-headers`. Note: I authored this file directly since I'm running as GitHub Copilot, not Claude Code — the workflow itself, and its `/workflows` progress view, only execute inside Claude Code CLI/Desktop.
